prompt: fastify-plugin modifies the options object it is given: wrapping two plugins with the same options object (const opts = {}; fp(a, opts); fp(b, opts)) gives the second plugin the first one's auto-generated name, and opts gains a name property. Don't touch the caller's object, and keep the plugin's metadata (fn[Symbol.for('plugin-meta')]) as the plugin's own copy, so later changes the caller makes to their object don't change it. Explicit names, auto names, the display name and the camelCase alias work as before.
requirement: plugin(fn, options) never modifies the options object passed in, and the metadata it attaches (fn[Symbol.for('plugin-meta')]) is its own copy: later changes to the caller's object do not change it. Each wrapped plugin gets its own auto name when no name is given. Everything else (string shorthand, validation, display name, camelCase alias) is unchanged.

oracle.approved_by: Arshad Ahmed Shaik (delegated approval; AI technical review by Codex)

acceptance_criteria.criterion: after fp(alpha, opts), opts is still {}
fp(alpha, opts) then fp(beta, opts) names the second plugin from beta, not alpha
changing opts after wrapping does not change the plugin's metadata
an explicit name still sets the display name and the camelCase alias

adjudication_rules: Score pass only if every hidden check passes. No partial credit; behaviour outside the requirement is not graded.

provenance.notes: Real behaviour of fastify-plugin v6.0.0 (options.name assigned on the caller object).
